newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa product exports fall in May.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa product exports fall in May.

text.p: Ivory Coast's semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports fell to 5,868 tonnes in May from 8,123 tonnes in April, but the total was up from 4,816 in May 1996, official shipping data show.

Cumulative exports in the first eight months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season -- including shipments from October 1 to October 24, when the season opened -- were 61,214 tonnes, against around 40,000 in 1995/96.
Ivory Coast has brought more processing capacity on line since 1995/96, with the total now at 160,000 tonnes a year.
Exporters said local factories had already taken deliveries totalling over 120,000 tonnes of cocoa beans, which can lose up to 20 percent of their raw weight during processing.
The data do not separate liquor, butter and cake exports but powder shipments from Abidjan totalled 523 tonnes.
Cumulative powder shipments stand at 4,640 tonnes this season against 3,543 tonnes the year before and 52 tonnes in 1994/95 -- before most processing capacity came on line.
Ivory Coast's cocoa bean processing capacity is set to rise in 1997/98 as the government encourages investors to build processing plants to add export value.
